title: Help that waits to be asked
statement: Keep help quiet and optional: glosses, notes and a few named helpers open only when the learner asks or with feedback, never as a constant guide or per-part buttons.
detail: Early drafts of a Grade 9 unit opening with a visible guide character and constant assistant behaviour were rejected, and the 6 October handover records that the required direction became a mature storytelling experience with quiet on-demand help (line 500); one of its design rules makes support quiet, optional and on demand (line 76). The rebuilt prototype offers three optional scripted helpers, one for a word's meaning or source context, one for a generic next step and one for a manageable way to begin, and during an independent attempt the meanings helper must not write the learner's claim or explain the interpretation being assessed (handover line 155; `g9/prototypes/review-build/DESIGN.md`, line 7).
against: On 7 October a visible guide character came back as the film's narrator and questioner, not as help (`g9/film/v07/README.md`, line 11), so the rejection held for help that interrupts, not for every on-screen guide. 'The help examples are scripted, not live AI.' (line 4612) and 'Whether they appear as three characters or different modes remains a design decision.' (line 2871), both in `g9/transcript/chat-transcript.redacted.txt`. The changes to the built lesson were proposed, not built or tried with students. The overload was a judgment, not a measurement, and no script checks the notes against the checkpoints, so the rule that a note never answers one is stated, not tested.

evidence.quote: Make support quiet, optional, and on demand. Avoid an assistant that constantly interrupts.
The visible Archivist concept and constant assistant behavior were not the desired approach. The required direction became a mature illustrated storytelling experience with quiet on-demand help.
offers a generic next step such as linking a claim to a word and explaining the connection.
helps the learner begin with a manageable action.
All three are optional scripted support in the current prototype, not a live adaptive tutor.
controls provide three distinct forms of scripted support; they do not pretend to be live AI.
also, given the nature of the age of the students , not to have 1 annoying assistant, but maybe 3 icons that each have their ownb type of help
three quiet, on-demand help icons could work better here
No unsolicited pop-ups or constant chatter. I’ll make that a visible option in the previews, with each icon clear about what help it gives.
Offer different kinds of help without making one authoritative guide the centre of everything (pp.9, 13).
My read: the younger feel comes mainly from how constantly the tutor directs the student.
Retrieval introduces the Archivist on a separate screen, then repeats the same instruction in a speech bubble. Put the instruction directly above the activity and let students start.
Bring a guide into view when the student requests help or receives meaningful feedback.
I wouldn’t remove scaffolding merely to make it look older; changing how much teaching students receive is a separate decision.
details that usually come up in classroom discussions — currently missing in the scripts
Pulled, never pushed: a quiet mark beside the line; the note opens in the side panel only if the student asks.
never answers a checkpoint; no context dumps.
removed per-part help on 2 Oct ("overloaded the learning").
Gloss words: dotted underline in ink. Tapped → the side panel shows the gloss. Never hover-only (tablets).
